Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

helpful adjective

of a person: obliging, ready to help

also obliging, kind (ready to help), unhelpful, very helpful of you, agreeable

classical

Cic. Rosc. Com. 18 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 13.21.2: homō

officiōsus, officiōsa, officiōsum

adjective · Declension on Wiktionary

obliging, ready to be of service

From officium, a kind service: ready to do people a good turn, especially those one owes respect to (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • cōmis, cōme — courteous, kind, obliging

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Balb. 36 (Lewis & Short); Ter. Hec. 5.3.39: benignō et lepidō et cōmī · Declension on Wiktionary

    Friendly and easy to deal with; more about manner than service.

  • commodus, commoda, commodum — obliging, agreeable

    also used · classical · Traupman 149, 156 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • cōmēs, benignī, facilēs, suāvēs hominēs esse dīcuntur quī errantī cōmiter mōnstrant viam

    people are called kind, generous, obliging and pleasant who show a man who has lost his way the road in a friendly mannerCic. Balb. 36 (Lewis & Short)

  • estne quisquam quī tibi officiōsior līberāliorque videātur?

    is there anyone who seems to you more obliging and generous?Cic. Rosc. Com. 18 (Lewis & Short)

See also useful, help, kind.
